game: PIT @ NE Week 3 2025, kickoff 2025-09-21 13:00 ET, outdoor Gillette; NE +1.5, total 44.5 (nflverse games.csv close). Rest/travel and open-to-close path not in the pack.

script.base: Market prices a one-score game: PIT -1.5, implied PIT 23.0 and NE 21.5 on a 44.5 total, so both quarterbacks stay in the plan and this is not a blowout. Base flow is competitive into the fourth quarter at a moderate pace. Pittsburgh should throw more than it pounds, because New England allows 3.11 rush YPC and only 2 runs of 10+ while pass YPA is 10.64/11.13/9.64 and CB Christian Gonzalez is out. New England should keep Rhamondre Stevenson on the ground, because Pittsburgh allows 4.40 YPC and 10 runs of 10+ with Alex Highsmith out.
script.flip1: PIT jumps up by two scores, kills the clock, and Jaylen Warren's carries spike while DK Metcalf and Calvin Austin III routes stall (the favorite-runs-late flip). NE then abandons the run, Stevenson carries die, and Drake Maye funnels throws to Stefon Diggs, Kayshon Boutte and Hunter Henry.
script.flip2: Backup corners and the missing PIT safety (DeShon Elliott) plus Joey Porter Jr. turn it into a pass-volume game, Metcalf/Austin and Diggs/Boutte/Henry all clear, and Warren's rush line dies. A live weather turn at outdoor Gillette, or a late inactive of Keion White or Derrick Harmon, is the other unpriced flip.

Gainwell rush 19 and 20, rec 4 and 16. Metcalf 83 and 20 — WR1 volume, one wipeout. Austin 70 and 22 on 173 air yards. Jonnu Smith 15 and 27 on 10 targets and -4 air (volume, no efficiency). Stevenson rush 15 and 54 (18/69) and rec 12 and 88; the 88 came out of only 28 air yards, so do not chase recyds 50.5 or rushrecyds 84.5. Henderson rush 27 and 10, rec a stable 24 and 30 on 8 targets. Diggs 57 and 32. Henry 66 and 9. Boutte 103 and 16. Maye 11/45 is a real carry share. Every stand-in line equals the two-game median, so form alone is a coin flip and the edge has to be matchup news the median does not include.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Stevenson finished under 34.5 because NE fell behind, Maye dropped back all day, and the 11 designed/scramble rushes plus Henderson and Gibson left Stevenson at 6 carries in the teens — the 15-yard week was the real role and the 54 was the outlier against a different front. Pittsburgh's 4.40 YPC was two games, not a law, and they schemed around Highsmith's absence. Metcalf finished under 51.5 because New England never shadowed him with Gonzalez (shell unknown; a zone team makes the hook and Jonnu Smith the matchup, not the outside corner), Scharping's absence shortened the route tree, Austin or Jonnu took the targets, and the 20-yard game repeated once PIT had a lead and ran. The counter is close to the read on both, which is why both are leans and the data check is a flag, not a sized bet.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a shootout and not a clock-kill stack: NE runs Stevenson into PIT's leaky front (Highsmith out, 4.40 YPC) while PIT throws to Metcalf into NE's pass funnel (Gonzalez out, 9.6–11.1 YPA) instead of pounding a 3.11 YPC run defense. Those two win together if the game stays within one score. Do not add Warren rush over, a total under with these overs, or Boutte/Austin overs that need explosive luck and the opposite script.
